content.text:
SrPrAlO4 (mp-1217963) is the best match. I compared four of the nine candidates against simulated patterns; the other five weren't simulated.

- **Peak positions match SrPrAlO4.** The observed peaks sit near 14.2°, 24.8°, 28.75°, 32.2° and 33.25° two-theta. SrPrAlO4's simulated peaks fall in the same order and spacing, about 0.3–0.5° higher from 24.8° upward. That fits a slightly larger lattice in the sample. A rough hand estimate for this kind of layered cell (about a ≈ 3.75 Å, c ≈ 12.6 Å) puts a reflection at 24.75°, matching the strongest observed peak.
- **Intensities don't match perfectly.** The observed peak near 24.8° is the strongest (100), but the simulation gives it only about 55 relative to its main peak near 32.5°. I've put that down to preferred orientation, but it is an assumption.
- **Other candidates checked.** SrZrO3 (mp-1020622), BaEuFe2O5 (mp-639347) and K2RbEuV2O8 (mp-1211828) all have their strongest peaks around 29–32°. None of them has anything at 24.8°, so none explains the strongest observed peak. They also don't account for the rest of the peaks, so I found no sign of a second phase among these.
